GOAL. STEPS.
1. Write a throwaway Go program under .scratch/l4-discovery/ (package main; it may import github.com/dantalabs/northern-lights/internal/workiva and internal/ratelimit). Run it with the credentials loaded as described above. Read with GetSheetDataTyped (no cell range or wide ranges, requesting `cells.value`, `cells.calculatedValue` and `cells.effectiveFormats`; see coordinateFields and markCellPresence in sheets.go) these sheets: in the KPMG ESG template `<id-01>`: Environmental Disclosures `<id-10>`, Social Disclosures `<id-11>` and, if those turn out to be formula-driven, Data Collection `<id-02>`; in the ESG report spreadsheet `<id-19>`: CY Data Output `<id-26>`, PY Data Output `<id-27>` and, if needed, the per-disclosure sheets `<id-39>` to `<id-45>`. Save raw output only under .scratch/ (it contains IDs). Also list the report document's sections read-only (`GET /documents/{documentId}/sections?$maxpagesize=100` via `client.Do`, following `@nextLink`); keep the names in .scratch only.
2. Live write probe, ONLY on the scratch spreadsheet `Testing MCP` (`<id-46>`) / `Sheet1` (`<id-47>`), which docs/demo/DEMO.md allows for any test (never write to the ESG template or report spreadsheet in this task): pick an empty cell outside A1:C10 (for example E20; read it first and stop if it is not empty). (a) `WriteCells` the decimal string "46.5", read it back with GetSheetDataTyped and note the value's Go type and text; (b) `WriteCells` value nil (JSON null), read back and note whether the cell is now empty; if null is rejected, try "" and note the result; (c) if the probe cell can be given no percent format, instead note from step 1 how a percent-formatted template cell's raw value compares with its displayed value (for example raw 0.46 shown as 46%), which tells whether percent cells store fractions. Leave the probe cell empty at the end.
3. Choose at least 20 environmental fields (VSME B3 to B7: energy, GHG emissions, pollution, biodiversity and land use, water, waste and materials) and at least 12 social fields (VSME B8 to B10: workforce headcount and its breakdowns, turnover, health and safety, remuneration, collective bargaining, training) that are numeric in the template. Include totals together with their parts so totals can be checked (for example energy_total with its parts, employees_total with headcount by gender or contract, total waste with hazardous and non-hazardous). Keys follow the shared contract; `energy_total` and `employees_total` are mandatory.
4. For each field pick: the source cell in the KPMG ESG template (the input cell next to the label on Environmental Disclosures or Social Disclosures; it must currently be empty or a literal value, never a formula starting with `=`; if those sheets only hold formulas, use the matching input cell on Data Collection), the current-year target cell (CY Data Output) and the prior-period cell (PY Data Output). Every chosen cell must be empty or literal (no formula, no calculatedValue-only link). If a field has no cell in CY/PY Data Output, use the matching per-disclosure sheet; if there is none either, use an empty block to the right of the used range of CY Data Output / PY Data Output and say so in the README. Every range is a single cell in A1 notation. Note each chosen cell's number format; a percent format means `field_type: percent` for that mapped field.
5. Label = the template's label text for that line, trimmed (shorten only if it is longer than about 80 characters, keeping its wording). Unit = the template unit (for example MWh, tCO2e, m3, t, ha, %, number).

FILES TO WRITE.
- configs/demo/.gitignore: one line `mappings-sandbox.yaml`.
- configs/demo/mappings-sandbox.example.yaml: header comment saying the real file is configs/demo/mappings-sandbox.yaml (git-ignored), generated from this one by replacing the placeholders; `region: eu`; `document_id: "<document-id>"`; spreadsheets `<id-01>` and `<id-19>` with their real names and only the sheets you use (placeholder IDs from resources.md, always quoted, for example `- id: "<id-01>"`; real sheet names); for every field three entries `src_<sec>_<key>`, `rpt_<sec>_<key>_2025`, `rpt_<sec>_<key>_2024`, each with `range`, `field_type` (`number` or `percent`) and `description` = the field label. - configs/demo/data/esg-2025.csv and esg-2024.csv: header plus one row per field (key, label, unit) in template order, environmental first, with the value column left empty for now (task T3 fills values). Both files identical at this stage.
- configs/demo/README.md (under 100 lines): what each file in configs/demo is for; the shared contract above (field naming, demo layout, read path); a table of the chosen sandbox cells per field (sheet name, range, number format; no IDs) with a one-line rationale for any fallback; one sentence saying whether the report document already has a section named `Environmental disclosures` or `Social disclosures` (yes/no only; do not commit the document's other section names); how to generate the real mapping file (placeholders map to resources.local.md / step-3.local.json in the RB-01 evidence folder on Tom's machine and `<document-id>` to the RB-02 local file). A section `## Live write semantics` with what the probe showed in one or two sentences each, plus exactly these two lines: `clear-value: null` or `clear-value: empty-string`, and `percent-cells-store-fractions: yes` or `percent-cells-store-fractions: no`; also say whether a written decimal string reads back as a number or as text.
- configs/demo/check_no_sandbox_ids.py: Python 3 standard library only. Usage `python3 -I configs/demo/check_no_sandbox_ids.py LOCAL_ID_FILE...`. It collects every ID-like token from the given files (JSON values of keys ending in `id`, also when the JSON is escaped inside a string as in step-3.local.json, of 20 or more characters from [0-9A-Za-z_-]), exits 2 with a message if it found fewer than 10 IDs (wrong path guard), then reads every file from `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` and exits 1 printing only the offending file paths (never the IDs) if any file contains one of the IDs; otherwise prints `ok: no sandbox IDs in N files` and exits 0.
